algorithm: {\text{This algorithm computes the priority for each bin as the negative of the remaining capacity after inserting the given item into the bin, assigning a very low priority (negative infinity) to bins that cannot fit the item, such that bins with the smallest remaining space after insertion receive the highest priority.}

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.where(bins >= item, -(bins - item), -np.inf)

    p = 1.5
    c = 0.1
    epsilon = 1e-12
    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    fit_mask = bins >= item

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.
    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
    epsilon = 1e-12
    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    fit_mask = bins >= item
    remaining_after = bins[fit_mask] - item
    # Use log of (bin_capacity / remaining_after + epsilon) to favor bins that balance utilization
    priorities[fit_mask] = np.log((bins[fit_mask] + epsilon) / (remaining_after + epsilon))
    return priorities

    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.
    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacities for each bin.

    c = 0.01

    ratios = remaining / (item + c + epsilon)

def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    epsilon = 1e-12
    priorities = np.zeros_like(bins)
    fit_mask = bins >= item
    remaining_capacity = bins[fit_mask] - item
    # Use log-transformed remaining capacity to penalize very small remainders
    log_remaining = np.log(remaining_capacity + epsilon)
    # Geometric mean scaled by item size and adjusted via log
    priorities[fit_mask] = item * np.sqrt(remaining_capacity + epsilon) / (log_remaining + epsilon)
    return priorities
